1.name: Lucia accuses him of firing the housekeeper
1.description: Lucia confronts the man about ending the housekeeper's employment.
evidence: "You fired her," Lucia said.

1.name: He defends giving notice after the house sale
1.description: He explains that he did not fire the housekeeper outright, but gave notice and severance because the house is being sold.
evidence: "I didn't fire her. I told her we couldn't keep her on once the house sold. Which it is going to. I gave her notice. I gave her severance. I —"

1.name: Lucia objects to the timing of the notice
1.description: Lucia points out that the housekeeper was given notice the day after the funeral, implying insensitivity.
evidence: "You gave her notice the day after the funeral."

1.name: They argue over keeping payroll for the empty house
1.description: He insists there is no reason to keep paying staff for a house no one will live in, while Lucia challenges his unilateral decision-making.
evidence: "What was I supposed to do, Lucia, keep her on payroll for a house no one is going to live in?"
"You could have asked me."
"It's not your decision to —"
"It's exactly half my decision, according to the will you keep waving around."

1.name: Asha interrupts the argument
1.description: Asha quietly tells them to stop, and the room falls silent.
evidence: "Stop."
Asha said the word quietly, and they both stopped,

1.name: Asha asserts control over the sale decision
1.description: Asha announces that they will not accept the offer that day and frames the refusal as a probate precaution.
evidence: "Here is what we are going to do," she said. "We are not going to accept the offer today."

1.name: Asha explains probate risk from closing too soon
1.description: Asha warns that closing before confirming the governing document could cloud title and expose both the estate and the executor.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano, before you respond, please understand I am not refusing on your sister's behalf. I am refusing on the estate's behalf, because as the attorney handling probate I cannot in good conscience let you close on the sale of the principal asset until I have satisfied myself that the document governing that asset is the operative one. If a later instrument exists, and it changes the disposition of the house, and we close before it surfaces, the buyer's title is clouded, the estate is exposed, and you personally as executor are exposed. Do you understand what I am telling you."

1.name: Mr. Serrano denies any later instrument exists
1.description: Mr. Serrano insists that no later document changing the house's disposition exists.
evidence: "There is no later instrument."

1.name: Asha requests time to verify the documents
1.description: Asha says that confirming the paperwork would only cost a few days.
evidence: "Then helping me confirm that costs you nothing but a few days."

1.name: Mr. Serrano says time is running out
1.description: Mr. Serrano rejects the delay, saying they do not have a few days.
evidence: "We don't have a few days."

1.name: presses to confirm codicil
1.description: The speaker insists that confirming the existence of a later instrument or codicil is necessary and asks Daniel to help.
evidence: "There is no later instrument."
"Then helping me confirm that costs you nothing but a few days."
"Then we will proceed."

1.name: Daniel resists delay
1.description: Daniel argues that there is no time to wait because the buyer's agent has made the deadline clear.
evidence: "We don't have a few days. The buyer's agent has been very clear. They have other properties. They —"

1.name: rejects Daniel's urgency
1.description: The speaker dismisses Daniel's concern, saying another buyer will come because the row house is valuable and the office will proceed anyway.
evidence: "Then they will buy one of those properties, and another buyer will come, because this is a row house in Spring Garden and you know what it's worth."
"I am not asking your permission, Mr. Serrano. I am telling you what my office is going to do."

1.name: orders house search and attorney call
1.description: Lucia announces that her office will search the house, call the attorney Rosa remembers, and verify whether a codicil exists.
evidence: "We are going to search the house for the document Rosa describes."
"We are going to call the attorney she remembers being on the phone."
"We are going to confirm or eliminate the existence of a codicil."

1.name: Daniel yields to search
1.description: Daniel briefly reveals panic, then regains composure and agrees to proceed cleanly.
evidence: Daniel stared at her.
"Fine. Of course. I want the same thing. I want this clean."

1.name: requests to attend search
1.description: Daniel asks to be present for any search of the house.
evidence: "I would like to be present for any search."

1.name: allows witnesses to attend
1.description: Lucia says Daniel, his sister, and Rosa may all be present, and identifies Rosa as a witness.
evidence: "You will be welcome. So will your sister. So will Rosa."
"Rosa was a witness. Rosa will be present."

1.name: Lucia's remark unsettles Daniel
1.description: Lucia's response provokes an uneasy reaction from Daniel and a suppressed laugh from Lucia.
evidence: Lucia made a sound that was not quite a laugh.
Daniel closed his mouth on whatever he had been about to say.

1.name: sets search appointment
1.description: Daniel asks when the search will happen, and Lucia schedules it for the next morning at ten with a paralegal and Rosa present.
evidence: "Fine," he said. "When."
"Tomorrow morning. Ten o'clock. I'll bring a paralegal. Rosa, can you be here?"
"Yes."

1.name: Asha agrees to the meeting
1.description: After a brief pause, Asha accepts the proposed arrangement and agrees to proceed.
evidence: He picked up his pen. He clicked it twice. "Fine," he said. "When."
"Tomorrow morning. Ten o'clock. I'll bring a paralegal. Rosa, can you be here?"
"Yes."
"Lucia, you'll be here?"
"I haven't left."
"All right."

1.name: Asha requests a house walkthrough
1.description: Asha closes the portfolio and asks to walk through the house that afternoon to orient herself.
evidence: Asha closed the portfolio without putting anything into it.
"I'd like a few minutes to walk through the house this afternoon, if no one objects. Just to orient myself."

1.name: Daniel offers to guide Asha
1.description: Daniel quickly volunteers to show Asha around the house.
evidence: "I'll show you around," Daniel said quickly.

1.name: Asha prefers Rosa as guide
1.description: Asha declines Daniel's offer and says she would rather have Rosa show her the rooms.
evidence: "Thank you, but I'd prefer Rosa, since she knows the rooms."
"Of course."

1.name: Daniel leaves the house
1.description: Daniel gathers his belongings carefully, announces a noon call, and exits the house.
evidence: He stood. He gathered his pad and his pen and his phone and his keys with the careful economy of a man who did not want to be seen rushing, and he said, "I have a call at noon. I'll see you tomorrow," and he left through the pocket doors and a moment later the front door opened and closed and the brass clapper rang once, faintly, in sympathy.

1.name: Lucia breaks down in apology
1.description: After Daniel leaves, Lucia exhales heavily, covers her face, and apologizes for not staying calm.
evidence: Lucia exhaled. It was a long exhale, and at the end of it she put her face in her hands and pressed her palms hard against her eyes.
"I'm sorry," she said into her hands. "I'm sorry. I shouldn't have — I told myself I was going to be calm."

1.name: Asha reassures Lucia
1.description: Asha tells Lucia that she was calm and that Daniel was the one struggling to hide his feelings.
evidence: "You were calm," Asha said.
"I wasn't."
"You were calmer than he was. He just had more practice hiding it."

1.name: Asha questions Lucia privately
1.description: Asha waits a moment and then asks Lucia if she has anything to say without Daniel present.
evidence: Asha let a moment pass. "Lucia. Is there anything you want to tell me without your brother in the room."

1.name: Lucia turns to Rosa
1.description: Lucia lowers her hands, regains composure, and looks to Rosa as if seeking support or confirmation.
evidence: Lucia took her hands away from her face. Her eyes were dry but the skin around them had gone pink. She looked at Rosa.

1.name: Lucia withholds her secret
1.description: Lucia refuses to reveal anything further, saying she is not ready to tell them yet.
evidence: "Not yet," Lucia said.

1.name: Lucia denies hiding anything important
1.description: Lucia insists she is not hiding anything that matters and only wants time to think.
evidence: "I'm not — I'm not hiding anything that matters. I just want to think."

1.name: Asha accepts Lucia's answer skeptically
1.description: Asha responds politely but does not believe Lucia's explanation.
evidence: "All right," Asha said again, and meant it, and did not believe her.

1.name: Rosa leads Asha through the house
1.description: Rosa guides Asha upstairs through the old Italianate house, naming the rooms as they go.
evidence: Rosa led Asha up the front stairs slowly, with one hand on the banister, and named the rooms as they passed

1.name: House history is revealed
1.description: The narration establishes the house's layout and the changing use of its rooms, including the dead señor's study, Estela's former bedroom, Daniel's old room, and Lucia's current sleeping room.
evidence: The house was a center-hall Italianate with a double parlor on the first floor, a dining room and butler's pantry and kitchen running along the back, and three stories above.

the señor's study, though the señor had been dead since 1998 and the room was now full of Estela Serrano's correspondence; the front bedroom, which had been Estela's; the back bedroom, which had been Daniel's growing up and was now an unused guest room with a stripped bed; Lucia's old room, where Lucia was currently sleeping, the door closed.

1.name: Asha enters the sewing room
1.description: Asha steps into the sewing room and pauses, taking in the space.
evidence: The sewing room was at the end of the hall, smaller than the others, with a single window that looked out onto a brick wall and a fire escape.
Asha stepped inside and stopped.

1.name: Sewing room is shown tidy
1.description: The sewing room is revealed to be very tidy, with a black Singer machine on a small table under the window.
evidence: The room was very tidy. A black Singer machine sat on a small table under the window.

1.name: Asha enters sewing room
1.description: Asha steps into the tidy sewing room and stops to take in the space.
evidence: Asha stepped inside and stopped.

1.name: Rosa identifies Lucia's work area
1.description: Rosa explains that this room was where Lucia handled her bills and kept important papers.
evidence: "This is where she did her bills," Rosa said.
"And the folder you mentioned. The bottom drawer."
"Yes. On the right."

1.name: Asha inspects desk without opening it
1.description: Asha studies the roll-top desk carefully but refuses to open it, keeping her hands behind her back.
evidence: Asha did not open the desk.
She put her hands behind her back, the way she had been taught in evidence class a lifetime ago, and looked at it.

1.name: Asha asks about room access after death
1.description: Asha asks whether anyone has entered the room since Lucia died, probing for possible tampering.
evidence: "Has anyone been in this room since she died?"

1.name: Rosa admits room was accessed
1.description: Rosa says she has dusted the room and that Miss Lucia sometimes sits there, indicating others have been inside.
evidence: "I have. To dust. Miss Lucia has. She sits in here sometimes."

1.name: Asha asks about Daniel's access
1.description: Asha specifically asks whether Daniel has been in the room, suggesting suspicion about his involvement.
evidence: "Daniel?"

1.name: Rosa reports uncertain room access
1.description: Rosa cannot say for certain whether Daniel entered, but recalls the room door being closed on Saturday and open earlier in the week.
evidence: "I do not know for certain. I came on Saturday to bring food and the door to this room was closed, and earlier in the week it had been open. That is the only thing I noticed."

1.name: Rosa confirms key always stayed in lock
1.description: Rosa says the desk key was always left in the lock because Lucia was not afraid of her children reading her papers.
evidence: "The key was always in the lock. The señora was not afraid of her children reading her papers."

1.name: Asha closes sewing room and postpones opening desk
1.description: Asha leaves the room, closes the door, and insists on returning with everyone present before the desk is opened.
evidence: Asha looked at the desk a moment longer. Then she stepped back into the hallway and pulled the sewing room door gently closed behind her.
"I'd like to come back tomorrow with everyone present before this is opened."
"Yes."

1.name: asks to reopen sewing room later
1.description: Asha says she wants to return the next day with everyone present before the sewing room is opened.
evidence: "I'd like to come back tomorrow with everyone present before this is opened."
she stepped back into the hallway and pulled the sewing room door gently closed behind her.

1.name: identifies October attorney
1.description: Rosa recalls the name of the other attorney who called in October and explains why the family chose him over Mr. Halloran.
evidence: "Stein. Or Stine. He was younger than Mr. Halloran. The señora said she did not want to use Mr. Halloran for the change because Mr. Halloran was Mr. Serrano's friend from the parish, and she wanted — she said the word — fresh eyes."
"Fresh eyes."
"Yes."

1.name: thanks Rosa and leaves room
1.description: Asha thanks Rosa, and the two women walk back down the hallway together.
evidence: "Thank you, Rosa."
Rosa nodded once. They walked back down the hallway together,

1.name: Rosa defends the boy
1.description: At the top of the stairs, Rosa stops Asha and asks her to understand that the boy is not bad but burdened by being made the man of the house too young.
evidence: At the top of the stairs Rosa stopped and put her hand lightly on Asha's forearm — not a grip, just a touch — and said, "Ms. Patel. The boy is not a bad boy. I want you to know that. He is a boy who was told he was the man of the house when he was twelve years old, and he has been trying to be that ever since, and his mother did not always know how to take it back from him. I am not asking you to be kind to him. I am asking you to know."
"I'll remember," Asha said.

1.name: Asha promises to remember
1.description: Asha accepts Rosa's warning and promises to remember what she has said about the boy.
evidence: "I'll remember," Asha said.
Rosa nodded again, and let go.

1.name: Asha leaves the house
1.description: Asha exits the house at 1:20 p.m. and heads into the neighborhood.
evidence: Asha left the house at twenty past one.

1.name: Asha sits in coffee shop without calling
1.description: After walking two blocks, Asha sits in a coffee shop with an untouched drink and delays calling anyone while thinking.
evidence: She walked two blocks before she found a coffee shop with a window seat and ordered a flat white she did not drink and sat with her phone in her hand and did not call anyone for ten minutes.

1.name: Asha reflects on father's portfolio and Daniel's warning
1.description: While sitting alone, Asha thinks about her father's portfolio and Daniel's statement that there is no later.
evidence: She was thinking about her father's portfolio. She was thinking about the way Daniel had said *there is no later

1.name: sits silently with phone
1.description: She sits holding her phone and does not call anyone for ten minutes.
evidence: sat with her phone in her hand and did not call anyone for ten minutes.

1.name: reflects on father's portfolio
1.description: She thinks about her father's portfolio while replaying the recent conversation and its implications.
evidence: She was thinking about her father's portfolio.

1.name: dwells on Daniel's denial
1.description: She fixates on Daniel's absolute denial that there was any later instrument, reading it as a deliberate version of the truth.
evidence: She was thinking about the way Daniel had said *there is no later instrument* — not *I'm not aware of one*, not *Mom didn't mention one to me*, but the flat, absolute denial of a man who had already decided what the truth was going to be.

1.name: recalls Lucia and Rosa's reactions
1.description: She remembers Lucia's and Rosa's contrasting gestures and statements from the earlier exchange.
evidence: She was thinking about Lucia's hands flat on the table, and the WHYY mug, and the small distance between *I didn't say anything about feelings* and *I'm not going to sit here and pretend I never heard Mom say things.* She was thinking about Rosa's reddened knuckles and the way she had said *I am not employed here anymore* as if it were a fact about the weather.

1.name: imagines locked desk and closed door
1.description: She thinks about a roll-top desk with a key in the lock and a door that has been opened and then closed, suggesting withheld information.
evidence: She was thinking about a roll-top desk with a key in the lock and a door that had been open and was now closed.

1.name: admits liking the others
1.description: She recognizes that she likes the people involved, despite not liking them equally.
evidence: She was thinking, also, about the thing she had been trained not to think about, which was that she liked these people. Not all of them, not in equal measure.

1.name: judges Lucia Rosa and Daniel
1.description: She interprets Lucia as needing an adult, Rosa as trusting her, and Daniel as frightened, revealing her growing emotional alignment with them.
evidence: But Lucia had looked at her like a person who needed an adult in the room, and Rosa had spoken to her like a person who had decided, on the basis of eight minutes of conversation, that she might be trustworthy, and even Daniel, behind his offense, had been visibly terrified, and Asha had a long-standing weakness for terrified people who would not admit it.

1.name: remembers supervisor's criticism
1.description: She recalls a past evaluation note accusing her of confusing compassion with neutrality.
evidence: *Confusing compassion with neutrality.* Her supervisor's words, written in the margin of an evaluation seven years ago.

1.name: recall supervisor's criticism
1.description: Asha remembers a past evaluation note accusing her of confusing compassion with neutrality and being weak for terrified people.
evidence: long-standing weakness for terrified people who would not admit it.
*Confusing compassion with neutrality.* Her supervisor's words, written in the margin of an evaluation seven years ago.
She had been twenty-eight then, and she had cried in the bathroom, and she had not forgotten.

1.name: call Halloran's office
1.description: Asha phones Halloran's office to ask about the Serrano matter and a possible colleague named Stein or Stine.
evidence: She picked up her phone and called Halloran's office.

"Tell him Asha Patel called about the Serrano matter. Tell him I'm asking whether his office has any record of a colleague named Stein or Stine who may have advised Mrs. Serrano in October. Tell him I'd like a callback today."

1.name: learn Halloran is unavailable
1.description: The receptionist tells Asha that Halloran is in a deposition until three and agrees to pass along her message.
evidence: "He's in a deposition until three," the receptionist said.
"I'll let him know."

1.name: reflect on financial pressure
1.description: After the call, Asha thinks through the buyer's agent, tax bill, and Daniel's likely hidden financial burden tied to the house sale.
evidence: She thought about the buyer's agent, whose pressure was real, and the tax bill, which was also real, and the bridge loan Daniel was almost certainly carrying on something, because men who needed a house sold in thirty days were never carrying nothing.

1.name: remember Lucia's hesitation
1.description: Asha recalls Lucia at a long table saying she just wants to think, reinforcing Asha's concern about the situation.
evidence: She thought about Lucia in a black sweater at the end of a long table, holding a mug from a public radio fundraiser, saying *I just want to think.*

1.name: leave the coffee shop
1.description: Asha pays for her coffee and departs after finishing the call and her reflections.
evidence: She paid for the coffee and left.

1.name: begin reviewing Serrano file at home
1.description: That evening, Asha sits in her Fairmount apartment with the Serrano file open and starts writing notes on a yellow pad.
evidence: That evening, in her own apartment in Fairmount, Asha sat at her kitchen table with the Serrano file open in front of her and a yellow pad of her own, and she wrote, in her steady left-hand print:
